title: MP Hizbullah appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Member of Parliament M. L. A. M. Hizbullah appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption today to provide a statement in connection with an ongoing inquiry into his assets and liabilities.

title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
byline: The current outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is on track to surpass the deadliest outbreak of the disease ever, the director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO) has said.

title: Sri Lankan student fatally stabbed by compatriot in Japan
byline: Police in Nagareyama City, Chiba Prefecture, have arrested an 18-year-old Sri Lankan national on suspicion of murder, after he allegedly stabbed a 21-year-old Sri Lankan man with a knife.

title: Eric Meyer sworn in as new U.S. Ambassador to Sri Lanka
byline: Eric Meyer has been officially sworn in as the new United States Ambassador to Sri Lanka at a ceremony held at the U.S. Department of State in Washington, D.C, the U.S. Embassy in Sri Lanka said.

title: UN Special Rapporteur concerned over proposed increase in judges’ retirement age
byline: The United Nations Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, Margaret Satterthwaite, has raised concerns over Sri Lanka’s proposed constitutional amendment to increase the retirement age of superior court judges, warning that the move could affect judicial independence and public confidence in the judiciary.

title: Colombia declares three days of mourning after deadly earthquake
byline: Colombia has declared three days of national mourning after a powerful earthquake killed more than 200 people as rescue crews race against time to find people trapped beneath the rubble.

title: Feels-like temperature rises as dry weather persists
byline: The feels-like temperature has risen to concerning levels in several parts of the country amid prevailing dry weather conditions, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Trump spokeswoman Karoline Leavitt to step down
byline: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, the youngest person to hold the role, will leave at month’s end, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday.

title: Woman steals ATM cards to fund her honeymoon
byline: A young woman who had stolen the ATM cards of a businessman at the instigation of her partner to spend for her honeymoon was arrested by the Athurugiriya police yesterday.

title: EU calls for decriminalisation of same-sex relations among key GSP+ recommendations
byline: The European Union, in its latest assessment of Sri Lanka’s situation for GSP+, has emphasised the need for the adoption of comprehensive anti-discrimination laws protecting ethnic and religious minorities and LGBTIQ+ persons, as well as the decriminalisation of consensual same-sex relations.

title: Indonesia Cultural Centre opens in Colombo
byline: The Embassy of the Republic of Indonesia in Colombo inaugurated the Indonesia Cultural Centre (ICC) on Wednesday, marking a new step in efforts to deepen cultural exchange and people-to-people relations between Indonesia and Sri Lanka.

title: South Korea’s Incheon airport becomes world’s busiest for global traffic
byline: South Korea’s Incheon has become the world’s busiest airport by international passenger traffic for the first time, new figures show.

title: Police say Malaysia operation to arrest Kanjipani was not a failure
byline: Police have rejected suggestions that the recent operation involving the apprehension of underworld figure “Kanjipani Imran” in Malaysia was a failure, saying the operation involved navigating the laws and procedures of a foreign country.

title: Ready to risk office for change, says President
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has said meaningful political and constitutional change requires taking risks, stressing that he is prepared to face the consequences of pursuing reforms.

title: Sri Lanka seeks Interpol Red Notices for 93 suspects hiding abroad
byline: Sri Lanka has obtained Interpol Red Notices for 93 suspects believed to be hiding overseas in connection with crimes committed in the country, Police Spokesman ASP F.U. Wootler said today.

title: Dogs can distinguish between emotions in a human face, study shows
byline: A peek inside dogs’ brains revealed man’s best friend can distinguish emotions in people’s faces, researchers at the ​University of Vienna have found, providing what they said ‌was the first ever evidence of such an ability.

title: Civil organisations form common platform to fight against 22A
byline: A group of civil organisations, with the blessing of the Joint Opposition and several others political parties, have formed a common front named ’Free Operations Centre’ to fight against the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution and to preserve multi party democracy in the country.

title: Test series in Sri Lanka won’t be easy, Gavaskar warns Indian team
byline: The two-match series in Sri Lanka won’t be easy, as Sri Lanka at home are a formidable team, Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar said.

title: Sri Lanka names squad for Women’s Asia Cup 2026
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket has announced a 15-member squad for the Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026, which will be held in the United Arab Emirates from August 28 to September 13.

title: Train services delayed on Main Line following breakdown
byline: All train services operating on Sri Lanka’s Main Line have been delayed following a train breakdown between the Ambepussa and Alawwa railway stations.

title: Education Ministry probes Physics paper mix-up at Ambalantota A/L exam centre
byline: The Ministry of Education has launched an investigation following the discovery of six packets containing tomorrow’s (14) G.C.E. Advanced Level Physics Paper I at an examination coordination centre in Ambalantota.

title: Over 1,000 foreigners arrested in cybercrime raids this year
byline: Sri Lanka Police have arrested 1,093 foreign nationals suspected of involvement in cybercrime and financial fraud during 24 raids conducted so far this year.

title: South Korea’s Incheon airport becomes world’s busiest for global traffic
byline: South Korea’s Incheon has become the world’s busiest airport by international passenger traffic for the first time, new figures show.

title: No exam papers opened or leaked: Exams chief
byline: Commissioner General of Examinations A.K. Indika Kumari Liyanage has categorically denied rumors of an examination question paper leak, assuring candidates that the examinations scheduled for tomorrow (14) will proceed as planned.

title: Govt. moves to break Sri Lanka’s exam-centred education culture
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has stressed the need to modernise Sri Lanka’s education and assessment systems by moving beyond an examination-centred model and placing greater emphasis on skills, creativity, experiential learning and holistic development.

title: Woman abandons 4-year-old girl in Wattegama
byline: A woman allegedly abandoned a four-year-old girl in Wattegama town today after arriving with the child in a three-wheeler, police said.
